issues.failure_explanation: For the stated Lagrangian, the Euler--Lagrange equations are D_i L^i_α - ∂H/∂u^α = 0, i.e. ∂L^i_α/∂x^i + (∂L^i_α/∂u^β)D_i u^β - ∂H/∂u^α = 0. The displayed formula instead uses K^i_{αβ}D_i u^β - ∂L^i_α/∂x^i - ∂H/∂u^α. For example, with one independent variable, L^1_1=(u^2)^2, L^1_2=0, H=0, the correct α=1 equation is identically 0, whereas the displayed equation gives an extra condition -2u^2 D_1u^2=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed continuous EL equations by the standard Euler--Lagrange expression D_i L^i_α - ∂H/∂u^α = 0, or by its correct expanded form, and adjust the surrounding K/conservation discussion.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous background statement of the multisymplectic Euler--Lagrange equations is incorrect; any argument relying on that displayed formula as the EL equations is unreliable. The discrete formulas later are derived separately.
issues.title: Continuous multisymplectic Euler--Lagrange formula is false
issues.why_classification: This is a local standard correction of one displayed formula; it does not require new proof architecture and the paper's discrete bicomplex results are not dependent on this incorrect continuous display.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, these equations may be weaker than the given system and so admit other solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed computation only shows that the given PΔE system is contained in the solutions of E^Δ(L)=0. It does not show that the Euler--Lagrange equations of L imply the given system. The paper itself notes, in the continuous discussion, that the constructed Lagrangian may yield weaker equations; the discrete converse omits this caveat and asserts that L is a Lagrangian form for the system.

issues.overall_effect: The advertised converse from a conserved multisymplectic form to a Lagrangian formulation of the system is unsupported; only one-way solvability is established.
issues.title: Converse Lagrangian claim confuses satisfying EL equations with equivalence
issues.why_classification: A supported resolution is a limited weakening of the converse claim. It preserves the construction but removes an advertised equivalence, so the defect is substantive and not merely a typo.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition, dDh u^β = Δ^j∧D_j u^β is a sum over all horizontal directions. In (lp), the index i is already used in (∂_{n^i}∫vol), so the product contains extra terms for j≠i. The asserted identity with only D_i u^β vol is therefore false for p>1 unless dDh u^β is reinterpreted as the directional difference Δ^i∧D_i u^β, which is not the operator dDh.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace dDh u^β in (lp) and related displays by the directional difference Δ^i∧D_i u^β, or introduce a directional difference operator and use it consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete multisymplectic Lagrangian (lp), the EL equations (el), the multimomentum theorem, and the examples relying on that Lagrangian are built on an ill-defined or incorrect form.
issues.title: Lagrangian form (lp) uses dDh u with a free direction index
issues.why_classification: The correction is local notational: it replaces a sum over directions by the intended single direction. The intended multisymplectic difference structure, examples, and theorem survive without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\mcI^{\vartriangle}$ is a projection and the difference variational bicomplex is exact, a difference version of equality \eqref{eq:ii} holds.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (eq:ii) is the differential identity σ=I(σ)-d_hτ, not the difference identity involving I^Δ and dDh. The difference analogue is not established within the proof of thm:added-3; it is asserted in the main text by assuming exactness of the difference bicomplex. Thus the proof of exactness at the last horizontal step relies on an unestablished or circular premise.
